questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of offline dynamic connectivity, edge lifetimes, and real-world constraints like memory and rollbacks.

## Key Concepts
- Segment-tree-over-time for edge lifetimes
- DSU with rollback to support deletions
- Handling parallel edges via unique IDs

## Code Example
```pseudo
buildSegTree(edges with [L,R))
dfs(node):
  apply all edges in node
  if leaf with queries: answer isConnected
  else traverse children
  rollback edges in node
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend to weighted edges or directed graphs?
- What are alternative online approaches?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design practical dynamic geometric data structures with real-world concerns like duplicates, deletions, and rebuilds.

## Key Concepts
- Dynamic KD-tree with lazy deletions
- Unique IDs for duplicates
- Nearest neighbor and k-NN search via bounding-box pruning and best-first traversal
- Rebuild thresholds to bound amortized costs

## Code Example
```javascript
// Skeleton: points with id, insert, erase, and query stubs
class Point { constructor(x, y, id) { this.x=x; this.y=y; this.id=id; } }
class KDNode { constructor(pt, left=null, right=null, min=null, max=null) { this.pt=pt; this.left=left; this.right=right; this.min=min; this.max=max; this.deleted=false; } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you choose and adapt the rebuild threshold in response to data skew? 
- How would you extend to support approximate NN for strict performance budgets?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to combine deque operations with real-time median maintenance, including duplicates and lazy deletions, under amortized log-time guarantees.

## Key Concepts
- Median maintenance with two multisets/heaps
- Lazy deletion to handle arbitrary pops from either end
- Balancing invariants to retrieve lower median for even sizes

## Code Example
```pseudo
class MedianDeque:
  left: Multiset // max-heap behavior
  right: Multiset // min-heap behavior
  delLeft, delRight: Map

  pushFront(x): insert into left; rebalance
  pushBack(x): insert into right; rebalance
  popFront(): mark in delLeft; prune; rebalance
  popBack(): mark in delRight; prune; rebalance
  median(): return max(left) if |left| > |right| else max(left)
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend this for a sliding window median over a fixed-size window?
- What are the memory implications of lazy deletions and how would you bound them over time?
